Surah al-Ma'un

Meccan, though its status is disputed, and it has seven verses.

﴿Have you seen the one who denies the Judgment?﴾ This is an interrogative intended to arouse the listener's eagerness to know who is being spoken of, and to express wonder at him. The address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). It has also been said that the address is to every person of reason. The verb "ra'ayta" (have you seen) here carries the meaning of "ma'rifah" (knowing, recognizing). It has also been read as "ara'aytaka," with the added particle of address.

The fa' in His words, Exalted is He, ﴿So that is the one who repulses the orphan﴾, is the response (jawab) of an elided conditional clause, on the basis that "that" (dhalika) is the subject (mubtada') and the relative pronoun (al-mawsul) is its predicate (khabar). The meaning is: "Have you considered the one who denies the Recompense or Islam? If you do not know him, or if you wish to know him, then he is the one who pushes the orphan away with a harsh push and drives him off with a vile rebuff." The use of the demonstrative (ism al-isharah), which draws attention to a description of the one indicated, in place of the pronoun, serves to signal the cause of the ruling and to alert the hearer, through what it carries of the sense of distance, to his remoteness in evil and corruption. It has been said that he is Abu Jahl, who was guardian of an orphan; the orphan came to him naked, asking him for some of his own property, and he repulsed him with a shameful push. It has also been said that he is Abu Sufyan, who slaughtered a camel, and an orphan asked him for some meat, so he struck him with his staff. It has also been said that he is al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, and it has been said that he is al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi, and it has been said that he is a stingy man among the hypocrites. It has also been said that the relative pronoun is general in its reference. And it has been recited as "yadca' al-yatim" (yada'u al-yatim), meaning: he leaves him and treats him harshly.

ومعنى ﴿وَلا يَحُضُّ﴾ أي: لا يحضّ أهله وغيرهم من الموسرين ﴿عَلى طَعامِ المِسْكِينِ﴾. وإذا كان حال من ترك حثّ غيره على ما ذُكِّر، فما ظنُّك بحال من ترك [ذلك] مع القدرة عليه؟

Translation:

"Nor urges" (﴿وَلا يَحُضُّ﴾): that is, he does not urge his family or others among the well-off ﴿to feed the poor﴾ (﴿عَلى طَعامِ المِسْكِينِ﴾). If the state of one who neglects to urge others to what has been mentioned is such, then what do you think of the state of one who neglects it while having the means to do it?

The fa' in His words, Exalted is He, ﴿So woe﴾ ...etc., is either to link what follows it to a deleted condition, as if it were said: "If what has been mentioned of not heeding the orphan and the poor is among the signs of denying the Religion and among the things that call for blame and rebuke, then woe ﴿to those who pray﴾." (p-204)

Commentary of Abu al-Su'ud (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on surah 107, verse 5:

﴿Those who are heedless of their prayer﴾ (heedless, unmindful, and not concerned with it).
﴿Those who make a show of [their deeds]﴾: that is, they show people their deeds so that people will see them and offer praise for them.

Abu al-Su'ud's commentary (Irshad al-'Aql al-Salim) on Surah 107, verse 7:

﴿And they withhold the ma'un (small kindnesses).﴾ That is: the zakat (obligatory almsgiving), or what is customarily lent among people. For indifference toward the orphan and the needy, given that it is as mentioned, entails indifference toward the prayer, which is the pillar of the religion; and ostentation (riya'), which is a branch of disbelief (kufr), and withholding zakat, which is the bridge of Islam, and bad dealing with people are all more deserving of this description. Or it is for the sake of ordering the supplication upon them with "woe" (wayl) on account of the vile deeds mentioned, and the placing of "those who pray" in the position of their pronoun, in order to lead, by this means, to the clarification that they have other vile deeds beyond what has been mentioned.

From the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Whoever recites Surah al-Din will be forgiven, provided he has been one who pays zakat."
